description: The pie chart visually represents the proportional distribution of various dialogue state tracking slots, likely from the dataset or model outputs discussed in the paper “Continual Dialogue State Tracking via Reason-of-Select Distillation.” The chart is divided into 15 distinct segments, each labeled with a slot name and its corresponding percentage. The largest segment is “from,” at 17.00%, followed by “to” at 14.50%, and “genre” at 13.50%. Other notable segments include “name” (5.20%), “size” (4.20%), “time” (4.10%), “intent” and “location” (both 3.80%), and “destination” (3.00%). Smaller segments include “city” (2.60%), “class” (2.40%), “range” (2.20%), “type” (2.00%), “beds” (1.30%), and “passengers” (1.10%). Each slice is color-coded and labeled with a percentage, with the labels connected via lines to their respective segments. One segment (likely “from”) is visually emphasized with a gray rectangular overlay, possibly indicating a focus or anomaly. The chart does not include a legend, relying instead on direct labeling. The segments are arranged in descending order of size, clockwise from the top-right, providing a clear visual hierarchy of slot importance or frequency.
